decision.question: Which class shape should the Notice/NoticeList/NoticeTray notification center use?
decision.ask: Which class shape should the Notice/NoticeList/NoticeTray notification center use?

options.text: A: NoticeTray reads NoticeList.items.length directly after every call it makes
options.say: A: NoticeTray reads NoticeList.items.length directly after every call it makes
caveats: Any future code that mutates the list without going through NoticeTray leaves the badge stale; nothing enforces calling the update.
options.caveat: Any future code that mutates the list without going through NoticeTray leaves the badge stale; nothing enforces calling the update.

options.text: B: NoticeList dispatches a change event; NoticeTray listens once and updates the badge
options.say: B: NoticeList dispatches a change event; NoticeTray listens once and updates the badge
caveats: Adds one new concept (a custom DOM change event) beyond the plain method calls the rest of the house style uses, though it reuses the existing .on() mechanism.
options.caveat: Adds one new concept (a custom DOM change event) beyond the plain method calls the rest of the house style uses, though it reuses the existing .on() mechanism.

options.text: C: Notice calls tray.sync() itself on dismiss; NoticeTray.sync() reads list.count from the live DOM
options.say: C: Notice calls tray.sync() itself on dismiss; NoticeTray.sync() reads list.count from the live DOM
caveats: Same staleness risk as A — any direct list mutation that skips tray.notify() must remember to call tray.sync() itself.
options.caveat: Same staleness risk as A — any direct list mutation that skips tray.notify() must remember to call tray.sync() itself.

decision.why: A three-class notification center's whole job is keeping the bell count honest; B is the only shape where a missed badge update is structurally impossible rather than a thing to remember, and it reuses the .on() pattern the house style already has for clicks.
